about: Every optimization candidate tried or considered (research/notes/2026/10-18-optimization-inventory.md section 2), wins and no-wins alike: verdict per engine, mechanism (why it helps or not), Lean decls for and against, missing why-theorems, premises, v1 evidence, general lesson, next action. Produced by workflow findings-r1 (4 read-only analysts) at main 6d5bf87; claims carry CONFIRMED/INFERRED/OPEN in their text. notes: append-only per-task additions to a finding field, one row per (entry, task) where entry is the finding's candidate text; a finding's full mechanism is its mechanism string followed by its notes with field mechanism, in array order (convention: docs/team/tools/ledger-merge.md, Lean Fw.Ops.LedgerMerge.distinct_notes_merge). Optional row fields: flag (the part:variant key the row decides), fResult (pass, unusable or model-bug; a model-bug row keeps its flag out of v2-proved, Lean Fw.Preset.falsified_not_mem), visClass (E, E-s, Q or L; required on the one row of every flag with a part.json visClass and equal to it, Lean Fw.Preset.Gen.classDisagreements_eq_nil_iff) and evidence (the source of the observation).

findings.candidate: batched (all reads, then all returned writes, one pass per frame)
findings.visual: open. E holds if no moved write changes a value that a later read in the same frame sees (premise NI, INFERRED true for the pilot: the hero writes --exit-opacity and pointer-events on .hero; the nav reads its own rect, the sticky profile and the track rect). Not E if batching also folds the hero-exit rAF trampoline, because the writes then land one frame earlier (v1 scroll-engine/01 note).
findings.mechanism: Style stage only. Total style passes per frame = [d ∧ (head is a read ∨ no write)] + #write-runs (PROVED: Fw.Parts.EngineScroll.total_style_closed). The engine merges only the hero's returned write run. The nav probe's two internal write→read pairs remain, so the pilot keeps 3 passes (1 with elements-skip): the moved pass comes back as the frame-end lifecycle update. Restyled elements are unchanged (same dirty sets, R2). Counter: trace.UpdateLayoutTree (det). A local run gave W equal, S equal (packages/measure-chromium/README.md:185). Core.frameWork counts [style touched] + forced, so it over-counts by 1 whenever the frame ends clean (last style access a read): PROVED Fw.Engine.frameWork_overcount; the faithful count forced + [endDirty] is Fw.Engine.frameWorkE (CONFIRMED: Chromium document.cc:2757-2762@f842f52 returns early when no style is dirty; WebKit Document.cpp:3042-3043@862f17d). Abstract closed form PROVED as Fw.Engine.flagTotal_closed: total = [d and first non-neutral access is not a write] + #write-runs (the form [d and head = R] alone fails at d, as = []). Golden finding: the forcedCountsBatched rows of Fw.Parts.Golden (engineSpecLines) are forced-only; read as totals they under-count every batched sequence that ends in a write by 1. Style totals faithful vs batched (d=true / d=false): pilot 4/3 vs 2/1 (forced alone says 1/0, so the batching saving is over-predicted by 1: 2, not 3), nav 3/2 vs 2/1 (forced says 1/0), [wS,rL] 1/1 vs 2/1 (forced says 1/0: batching is worse by 1 at d, not equal), [rL,wL,rL] 2/1 vs 2/1 (forced says 1/0: no saving, not 1). Layout totals for the same rows move the same way for [rL,wL,rL] (2/1 vs 2/1). No golden row was edited (the rows are labelled forced counts); the Parts proofs that should move to frameWorkE are listed in docs/team/handoffs/why-core-lessons.md. Under the frame-end pass (frameWorkE) batching can also add a pass: it is worse exactly when the frame starts dirty and its first flag access is a write followed by a read (total_batch_worse_iff). The golden forcedCountsBatched rows are forced passes only: read as totals the pilot batched style row is 2/1 (dirty/clean start), not 1/0, against 4/3 faithful (Fw.Parts.Golden.pilot_batched_rows_forced_only).

findings.v1Evidence: ../fastwork-com-web-optimize/fixes/scroll-engine/README.md /01 measure/mutate engine: forced style+layout 92 → 69 ms within noise, LoAF +25 ms ('WORSE', below the A/A noise), 'iE's forced total stays about the same', frames >20 ms are 'per-frame style and paint cost, which batching doesn't remove'; parked. v2 local: Chromium batched W equal, S equal (packages/measure-chromium/README.md:185-186); WebKit 164 → 145 RecalculateStyles (packages/measure-webkit/README.md:272), local debug only.
findings.lesson: Reordering reads before writes saves a style pass only for each extra write run it merges. A pass whose write ends the frame comes back as the lifecycle update. Predict with total = [d∧head-read] + #write-runs, not with forced alone. Count totals, never forced passes alone: a batched forced count of 0 can hide a frame-end pass.

findings.candidate: observers (KD#1): replace per-frame rect reads with IntersectionObserver/ResizeObserver
findings.visual: not-equal per frame. Blink delivers IO by posted task (one frame late). IO thresholds are discrete, so continuous outputs (exit opacity, morph) cannot come from IO. An IO-based hit test ignores stacking and occlusion. E only at settled states, and for boolean thresholds through a sentinel (HeroExitOpt.sentinel_iff_pointerOff) up to that lag.
findings.mechanism: It would save forced style/layout on main. Removing one reader removes a pass only if no later reader in the frame pays the same flush. The nav's elementFromPoint and rect reads stay every frame, and WebKit's scrollY forces layout (LocalDOMWindow.cpp:1466-1479@862f17d). New cost: IO compute in every lifecycle (Blink local_frame_view.cc:1148-1189; WebKit Page.cpp:2367). Blink posts delivery (intersection_observer_controller.cc:90-105). WebKit calls back inside the update, then lays out again (Page.cpp:2337, 2399). Counters: trace.IntersectionObserverCompute (det), WebKit ObserverCallback. Removing one checking read saves a pass only when the flag is dirty at the read and the next flag access after it is a write (PROVED: Fw.Parts.EngineScroll.total_remove_read).

missingWhy.statement: Observer timing: let $w$ be a write computed by an observer callback from the layout of frame $k$. Blink: $w$ is first visible in frame $k+1$. WebKit: $w$ is visible in frame $k$, and the update pays one extra style/layout pass when $w$ dirties them. Hence on crossing frames $\mathrm{obs}_v(k) = \mathrm{obs}_o(k-1)$ in Blink, and $\mathrm{passes}_v(k) = \mathrm{passes}_o(k) - \mathrm{forced}_{\mathrm{removed}} + [\mathrm{crossing}(k)]$ in WebKit.
missingWhy.needs: a per-frame step order (rAF → layout → observation → final layout) and a delivery mode per engine

missingWhy.statement: Observer dominance condition: $W_{\mathrm{obs}} \preceq W_o$ on frame $k$ iff no remaining reader in the frame checks the flag the removed read checked, and $\mathrm{crossing}(k) = 0$. Over a run, a strict gain needs $\#\{k : \mathrm{crossing}(k)\} < \#\{k : \text{read removed}\}$.
missingWhy.needs: the reader-removal lemma, the observer step above, and an IO compute unit in Stage (props or a new observe stage)

findings.v1Evidence: No 'observers' engine was built in v1 (only the flag proposal, ../fastwork-com-web-optimize/research/knowledge-distillation/README.md:584). The nearest experiment, ../fastwork-com-web-optimize/fixes/scrollcb-g0/README.md (an IO gate that idles off-screen callbacks), was rejected: 'no style or layout pass goes away, because the pending flush is paid by the next reader'. Chrome forced style 232-243 → 230-231, forced layout 123-124 → 125-126; Simulator layouts overlap (843-886 vs 835-875).
findings.lesson: Replacing one per-frame read saves nothing while another reader in the same frame pays the same flush. Observers win only for threshold outputs whose crossings are rarer than frames. They add per-target compute and a delivery lag (Blink) or a lifecycle repeat (WebKit).

findings.candidate: write-on-change (toggle is-on-dark only when it changes)
findings.visual: E: changed_write (the final class is the same)
findings.mechanism: No stage changes. A classList.toggle(c, b) that matches current presence never updates the class attribute in either engine (Blink dom_token_list.cc:148-157@f842f52; WebKit DOMTokenList.cpp:139-161@862f17d), so there is no style invalidation to save. The original also diffs classes in Svelte set_class (snapshot chunks/BSBv9QXB.js:2841-2853) and in signal equality, and every TS variant already writes on change (nav.hitTest/index.tsx:40-45). Only a JS DOM call is saved, which no CI counter sees (FunctionCall counts callbacks). writeOnChange_le is true, but it counts a no-op toggle as a Change. The engine already drops a class toggle that does not change presence, so always-toggle and write-on-change give the same frame (PROVED: Fw.Parts.NavHitTestOpt.toggle_noop): no-win in both engines.
premises: DOMTokenList.toggle(token, force) is a no-op when presence already equals force: CONFIRMED in both engines (raw files at the pins)
the original's class binding diffs per key: CONFIRMED snapshot chunks/BSBv9QXB.js:2841-2853 (the alias U → set_class is INFERRED)
every TS variant returns no writer when the class is unchanged: CONFIRMED apps/site/src/parts/nav.hitTest/index.tsx:40-45
findings.v1Evidence: Listed in KD#1 as part of the winning bundle ('write on change only'; ../fastwork-com-web-optimize/research/knowledge-distillation/README.md lesson 1). No isolated v1 measurement: it was always bundled with nav-hit-test and nav-hit-cache.
findings.lesson: Before claiming a saving from skipping no-op writes, check the engine and framework no-op paths (DOMTokenList toggle with force, Svelte class diff, equal inline values). When they already dedupe, the saving is zero. Do not hand-dedupe writes the engine already dedupes; check the engine no-op path first.
findings.next: Record as no-win and take it off the candidate list (it is already in the faithful port). Prove the no-op toggle equality, and add a no-op rule to the engine model's Change constructor so future candidates are not credited for engine-deduped writes.

findings.candidate: hero-exit-threaded (v6, KD#2): JS --exit-opacity writer → per-consumer CSS scroll-driven animations, plus an IO sentinel for pointer-events
findings.visual: E-s at the computed-value level under RG11 (consumer_eq_s; exact at integer scroll offsets, otherwise within the progress quantum: 1/(16R) in Chromium, 1 px on WebKit's main thread). Pixels: WebKit E in the v1 Simulator except a 30 px top band (78 levels). Chromium not-equal under the pixel rule (v1: ≤ 6 levels on 15-42k px, 1 device-px copy shift from GPU blending and snapping), so Q at best: PathPremises.raster_path fails there (INFERRED).
findings.mechanism: Removes the rAF script (FireAnimationFrame/FunctionCall −1 per scrolled frame, det), the forced track-rect read, and the inherited --exit-opacity restyle of about 230 descendants (style units, R2). Chromium: opacity and transform go to the compositor; blur stays on main (bit 12, compositor_animations.cc:405-417), so paint and raster remain. In the lane every BeginFrame keeps a style pass, so the UpdateLayoutTree count does not drop, and elementCount is quarantined (C-3). WebKit: all animations threaded (wk_all_comp), web-process work drops, the UI process and the layer count grow. PROVED (toy rasters): raster_path fails for a half-pixel translate (snap 0 vs resample 128, Fw.Engine.raster_path_fails_fracXf) and for group opacity 1/2 over child 3/10 (38 vs 39, Fw.Engine.raster_path_fails_fracAlpha), so PathPremises needs C5 and C4 (Fw.Engine.PathPremises5, shown_eq5). A compositor move adds the comp stage, so it is never framewise <= (Fw.Engine.comp_move_not_le): mixed or noClaim when the original pays no comp, trade only when it already does. Under frameWorkE both trades stand (cr_real_tradeE, wk_tradeE). Given the premise that each animated consumer adds a composited layer, the claim cannot be dominates on either engine, WebKit included (Fw.Engine.claim_ne_dominates_of_layers): at best trade.

missingWhy.statement: The lane cannot see the style saving: in lane mode $V.\mathrm{passes}(\mathrm{style}) = O.\mathrm{passes}(\mathrm{style})$ while $V.\mathrm{units}(\mathrm{style}) = N_{\mathrm{anim}} < 1 + |\mathrm{inh}(.\mathrm{hero})| = O.\mathrm{units}(\mathrm{style})$. The only count that maps to units is elementCount, which is quarantined, so `noMoreWork` cannot confirm it (`quarantined_unsound`).
missingWhy.needs: R2 inherited fan-out units in crOrig (it currently counts one change per consumer, which undercounts the original)

missingWhy.statement: Edge-frame cost on WebKit: the frames where the filter goes $\mathrm{none} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{blur}(\epsilon)$ or opacity crosses 1 pay layout: $\mathrm{layout} \in \mathrm{stages}_{wk}$ on those frames, $\#\mathrm{edgeFrames}_v \ge 1$ per rest→live switch
missingWhy.needs: tabling WebKit.opacityCross1_layout and a filter-presence clause for the variant's start and park frames

WebKit: a transform animation on .hero-copy made the accent repaint about 1.4× as often; none → blur(0.009px) costs one Layout; the 30 px top band was 78 levels off, so the writer was kept there; P-081: go-live-from-rest frames cost more than C's.
findings.lesson: Moving main-thread work to the compositor is a trade, never dominance. In the CI lane style passes stay one per frame, so only script and the quarantined elementCount drop. Compositing also changes rasterization, so value-level E-s is not pixel E.
findings.next: Record as a trade in both engines. Refine Visual.raster_path for fractional translate and opacity, and decide whether the Chromium arm is Q or gated to WebKit (as v1 did). On CI, run rewrite+hero-exit-threaded and check FireAnimationFrame <o (det) and compositeFailedBits bit 12 only on the blur animations. Add R2 units and Resident layers to HeroExitOpt.

findings.candidate: strip (cd-strip, KD#12): 10 will-change faces per digit -> one 12-entry strip
findings.visual: E inside the clip window, every env/width/instant (strip_visSame from strip_shows_same); no premise beyond the restated geometry
findings.mechanism: Saving is resident: one will-change layer per face (compositing_reason_finder.cc:76-137@f842f52) becomes one per digit, 80->8 (hero_layers). Per frame, stage passes are equal (strip_passes_eq); only units drop from 10r to r (strip_units), and units are visible only in the quarantined UpdateLayoutTree.elementCount (C-3). CI can see census.layers (<o) and nothing per frame. New cost: 12 instead of 10 cells backed per digit (strip_backing_gt, full-layer rule INFERRED), so the label is trade. On WebKit, layers exist only under the Normal policy (wk_owns). The v1 re-entry paint drop comes from coverage-rect backing detach (GraphicsLayerCA.cpp:3035-3060@862f17d), which is not modelled. Scheduling confound: if the TS strip keeps a shared-loop subscriber (k > 0 script units on still frames) the still frame is not <= the original in any engine (sub_still_not_le); the strip win needs the subscriber removed.

full-layer backing rule (each layer backs its whole box): INFERRED

findings.lesson: Fewer layers is a resident win, not a per-frame win: passes stay equal and only a census can see it, and any growth in backing makes it a trade. A layer variant must not also change scheduling.
findings.next: Split the TS flag into strip (layers only, faithful timer) and a separate clock flag. Run chromium-counts census.layers on CI. Prove the WebKit re-entry paint theorem once the coverage-rect rule is in WebKit.lean.

findings.candidate: cd-roll-ca: spring roll replaced by a WAAPI transform animation with sampled keyframes
findings.visual: E-s only at one fixed cadence, given that frame times equal the keyframe sample times (R5 clock premise). Not E across cadences: the spring integrates in min(left,16) ms slices (springLoop), so its path depends on how time is split into frames.
findings.mechanism: The roll moves from a per-frame rAF transform write (Chromium `direct`: script, style, props, commit) to a compositor transform animation (transformAnim_comp). On WebKit the legacy CA path accepts keyword-linear keyframes; legacy_rejects covers only linear() with points and steps(). Chromium saves script (FireAnimationFrame, FunctionCall: det) and the commit (cc.Commit: det) on every roll frame; lane style stays 1 per BeginFrame (F1). Each roll adds one start (style, props, commit). WebKit's web process does 0 work per frame only while nothing else renders: every rendering update ticks and invalidates every relevant animation (AnimationTimelinesController.cpp:149-177, KeyframeEffect.cpp:2129-2131@862f17d). CA asks for 80-120 Hz (PlatformCAAnimationRemote.mm:611-612), a UI-process cost no counter sees. The spring path depends on the frame split (two 8 ms steps differ from one 16 ms step, spring_split_differs), so no fixed WAAPI curve is E across cadences: E-s at one cadence only.

missingWhy.statement: E-s at a fixed cadence: $\forall \delta>0, k:\ \operatorname{waapiLin}(P_\delta, k\delta) = \operatorname{spring}^{(k)}_\delta$, where $P_\delta$ holds the spring states sampled at $k\delta$ as keyframes with linear easing between them

findings.visual: E against the drift-free original (Chromium-style re-arm from the scheduled time); the v1 chain aims at the original's own phase. Not equal on WebKit under thermal or low-power timer alignment: there the original skips one shown second about every 50 s and the variant does not. That makes it a correction, not a parity. findings.mechanism: There is no stage to save: both arms fire one timer and write the digits once per shown second. WebKit re-arms a repeating timer from its actual fire time and aligns fire times to a coarser grid in low-power or thermal mode (DOMTimer.cpp:436-448, Page.cpp:3072@862f17d). The original therefore drifts about 20 ms per fire (1000/20 = 50 s per skip). The chain keeps 60 fires per minute against 58.92, which is +1.8 % timer work at Serious. The CI lanes have no thermal mode, so no counter sees either effect. The v2 TS per-frame subscriber version adds 1 rAF callback every frame. Same run, same work: the per-second timer passes are equal, so there is no work claim (same_run_noClaim via Fw.Engine.resident_only_noClaim); the change is a visual fix, not an optimization.

On iPhone WKWebViewIOS.mm:1100-1104@862f17d clears allowedTouchTypes but keeps scrollEnabled, so a recognized pan and its deceleration continue (UIKit part INFERRED). Classic scrollbars: the lock would shift the layout by the scrollbar width without scrollbar-gutter: stable (layout_box.cc:1474-1494@f842f52, LocalFrameView.cpp:7322-7333@862f17d), so the arm locks only on overlay scrollbars. The arm reads the scrollbar kind once per activation, before its first style write, because clientWidth forces style and layout (element.cc:2622-2633@f842f52, Element.cpp:1632-1635@862f17d).

findings.visual: Equal opacity, blur and scale on every frame under the WAAPI premises (interp_eq, threaded_eq, retarget_from_shown). findings.mechanism: MEASURED (CI webkit-sim, iOS Simulator 430x775, lag and cost passes; reference const-bounds run 39846941236, flag run 39846909558, bundle with platform:fade-threaded run 39846948148): Composite per frame on the open push 236-552 ms against 151-213 ms (cost-report: higher, ranges do not overlap); close push 142-250 against 107-148 ms (overlap); Paint per frame, frames and resized layers overlap; new layers per 100 reads on the close push 100 against 0. PROVED (Fw.Parts.MorphPanelThreaded): the variant's tick costs style only (variant_stages, variant_drops) and keeps the nav write (recalc_same), adds no layer when the panel is composited (layer_budget); the stage model has no Composite stage. INFERRED: the blur moves from Paint to the compositor, which runs on the CPU in the Simulator, on a panel whose box is already constant (const-bounds class), so the rise is UNKNOWN
missingWhy: Composite cost is not in the stage model (Fw.Engine.WebKit stages end at paint), so the Composite rise on the open push has no Lean theorem; the cause is UNKNOWN
Compositor cost is not measured on a real GPU: the Simulator has none, and the open push has only 2-4 frames per pass

findings.mechanism: On the CI macOS Playwright WebKit wheel lane no drive a user produces can overlap a moving drawn scroll with the open morph: the site prevents every wheel while the morph is open and L restores scrollY after each scroll event; the pull drive adds a scroll event and a pull-and-restore per frame, drawn at the lock; strictly changing scrollY was not delivered. MEASURED (run 40032804511, 3 mac jobs): the push arrived at scrollY 5098 against maxY 5102 in 36 of 36 pull runs (0 atEnd, 0 stalled, 0 refused); scroll events in the open phase 60.2 to 62.7 per run. INFERRED: each frame is drawn at the lock because the site restore runs in a rAF after the page rAF (Page.cpp:2295 and :2330 @862f17d); no paint-position reading was taken. The rewrite's open-phase counts still overlap the original's with scroll work in every frame. Lean: Fw.Measure.WebKitLagPhase acceptPull (atEnd and stalled refusals, golden checked); acceptPull in macreport.mjs is a TS stand-in checked against that golden. Not claimed for iOS touch: a pan that began before the morph opened cannot be cancelled by touchmove there (WKContentViewInteraction.mm:4239-4245 @862f17d, INFERRED).
missingWhy: Whether UIKit's deceleration and the site's restore fight at the page end on iOS touch (task touch-lock-page-end).
premises: Drawn at the lock is INFERRED from rAF order, not read from a paint position.
findings.lesson: A site that restores the position after every scroll event cannot be driven into a moving drawn scroll by a page script; a drive that pulls and restores adds the event work but not the movement.

findings.mechanism: CONFIRMED (source, Lean Fw.Parts.HeroContainOpt): Chromium ObjectIsRelayoutBoundary returns true for layout plus size containment once the guards pass (layout_object.cc:1535-1538@f842f52; guards :1441-1531, the hero is a block-track child, a flex container, self-painting, with no out-of-flow descendant escaping it); WebKit isLayoutBoundary returns true for layout plus size containment (RenderObject.cpp:530-531@862f17d) and false for the base hero (overflow visible, :536-539). The marking walk starts at the container, so a dirty hero box roots at the view (outside_view). Chromium keeps a list of subtree roots and a walk reaching the view makes a full layout (local_frame_view.cc:1676-1723); WebKit keeps one root and two disjoint roots make a full layout (LocalFrameViewLayoutContext.cpp:701-753). So a frame with only hero-internal sources lays out the hero subtree (drawIn_flag_hero), any outside source or the hero box itself gives a full layout (drawIn_outside_full, cr_outside_full, wk_outside_full). notes.entry: hit-skip (skip the probe while morph > 0.2)
notes.text: why-engines: every elementFromPoint runs UpdateAllLifecyclePhasesExceptPaint up to kPrePaintClean with no clean early return (layout_view.cc:149-151, local_frame_view.cc:2199-2203, 2395-2452@f842f52), so each hit adds a props (pre-paint) pass: crWorkH_props_ge_hits, and skipping one probe is -1 props pass (hitSkip_props). CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: elements-skip (elementsFromPoint with an allow-list, no pointer-events write)
notes.text: why-engines: list-based requests avoid the hit-test cache (hit_test_cache.cc:54-56, hit_test_request.h:146-152@f842f52) and visit every layer of a penetrating list (hit_test_result.cc:565-586), so hitUnits(single) <= hitUnits(list), strict iff the first hit is not the last candidate (single_lt_list_iff). CONFIRMED. why-engines (model correction): an inherited pointer-events change sets SetShouldInvalidatePaintForHitTest per box (layout_object.cc:3477-3480, 5211-5219@f842f52), but pre-paint repaints the box's painting layer (pre_paint_tree_walk.cc:285-302), so the paint units are the distinct painting layers, not the boxes: 1 <= peUnits <= |inh| (pePaintUnits_bounds), = 1 when the nav shares one layer (pePaintUnits_shared). The stated >= |inh| fan-out over-counts. CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: hero-exit-threaded (v6, KD#2): JS --exit-opacity writer → per-consumer CSS scroll-driven animations, plus an IO sentinel for pointer-events
notes.text: wktr-p1p4 (scroll_comp_ride, MEASURED): on WebKit the threaded scroll-driven animations still tick and restyle their targets in every rendering update, so the old wkVar_eq and wk_var_exact (variant style passes 0 and units 0) were false. MEASURED (task wktr-p1p4, WKTR of the iOS 26.5 Simulator on macos-26, CI run 39075991405, 3 jobs x 3 passes, fixtures in packages/measure-wktr/fixtures): a transform animation on animation-timeline: scroll(root) costs exactly 1 style recalc per rendering update (53 of 53, then 159 of 159 with two idle updates per step); the scroll-only control 0; the same animation on the document timeline (accelerated) 0; classes by fwcore (kMax 4, tMax 24) over 9 runs: styleRecalcs deterministic in all three; a JS rAF write is quarantined (0.74 to 0.93 per update).

notes.entry: hero-exit-threaded (v6, KD#2): JS --exit-opacity writer → per-consumer CSS scroll-driven animations, plus an IO sentinel for pointer-events
notes.text: Restated (hero-exit-restate): wkVar is rebuilt on webkitX as a fold of withAnim over the N+3 (target, animation) pairs; under the premise WktrStyleRate.Holds (registry id wktr_scroll_timeline_restyle, lane wktr-fixtures.yml) the variant's scrolled frame has style passes 1 and style units N+3 (wk_var_exact), the original's 1 and 2N+4, so wk_trade still holds against wkOrigChanges with layered targets (lo != none) but not for every change list (wk_trade_not_general: against an empty callback the variant does more main-thread work). Golden hero-exit.jsonl: WebKit RecalculateStyles and styleRecalcs move from <o to <=o (7 vs 12 units at gN=4); every other row unchanged; the claim stays trade.

notes.entry: strip (cd-strip, KD#12): 10 will-change faces per digit -> one 12-entry strip
notes.text: why-engines: backing is kept iff the layer meets the coverage rect, does not allow detaching, or is pinned by a transform animation (GraphicsLayerCA.cpp:3036-3061@862f17d); a re-attach calls setNeedsDisplay over the whole bounds (PlatformCALayerRemote.mm:719-731, RemoteLayerBackingStore.mm:240-243) and a fresh store has no front buffer, so the first display is full (ImageBufferSet.cpp:42-50). A face that leaves and re-enters C repaints its whole area (face_reattach); the strip always meets C and pays 0 (strip_no_reattach). The full repaint on re-attach, INFERRED before, is now CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: cd-roll-ca: spring roll replaced by a WAAPI transform animation with sampled keyframes
notes.text: why-engines (statement refuted as written): an accelerated animation is ticked, and so restyles its target (WebAnimation.cpp:1558-1582, KeyframeEffect.cpp:1731-1735, 127-135@862f17d), only when its timeline is updated; a document timeline updates only when an update was scheduled for it, and a fully accelerated running effect schedules none (DocumentTimeline.cpp:190-205, 350-399; KeyframeEffect.cpp:2724-2745). So a rendering update alone adds no style for cd-roll-ca (time_comp_no_ride); it rides along exactly when ticks(time, upd, sched) (ride_iff), i.e. when another main-thread animation keeps the document timeline scheduled. CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: CM / compositor-morph (PR-030): transforms on a scroll timeline, rounded box from 4 corner clippers
notes.text: why-engines: a scroll timeline answers yes in every update while its source is connected (ScrollTimeline.cpp:291-298@862f17d), and the timelines controller ticks each of its animations (AnimationTimelinesController.cpp:138-178), whose tick invalidates the target's style even when accelerated (WebAnimation.cpp:1558-1582, KeyframeEffect.cpp:2129-2132, 1731-1735, 127-135). So the CM style floor holds in WebKit: one style pass and +1 style unit per updating frame (scroll_comp_ride). CONFIRMED. This contradicts the golden P1 'scrollDriven RecalculateStyles = 0' and P4 'styleRecalcs = 0' predictions (WebKit.lean golden rows), which were never measured on a scroll-driven fixture.

notes.entry: CM / compositor-morph (PR-030): transforms on a scroll timeline, rounded box from 4 corner clippers
notes.text: MEASURED (task wktr-p1p4, WKTR of the iOS 26.5 Simulator on macos-26, CI run 39075991405, 3 jobs x 3 passes, fixtures in packages/measure-wktr/fixtures): a transform animation on animation-timeline: scroll(root) costs exactly 1 style recalc per rendering update (53 of 53, then 159 of 159 with two idle updates per step); the scroll-only control 0; the same animation on the document timeline (accelerated) 0; classes by fwcore (kMax 4, tMax 24) over 9 runs: styleRecalcs deterministic in all three; a JS rAF write is quarantined (0.74 to 0.93 per update). The source reading is right and the goldens were wrong: P1 RecalculateStyles and P4 styleRecalcs for scrollDriven are regenerated from =0 to =o (Fw.Engine.WebKit.style_rate_model, style_rate_old_refuted).

notes.entry: g0.0f: the bar's colour from two flat GPU layers plus a clip shape (Safari only)
notes.text: why-engines: a layer that neither draws content nor delegates display drops its backing store (PlatformCALayerRemote.mm:224-228@862f17d); a resize re-creates the backing parameters (:596-608, 333-355), which clears the store and dirties the whole layer (RemoteLayerBackingStore.mm:139-152), and a layer with no store has nothing to dirty (:357-375). So simple layers hold 0 kpx and paint 0 on resize (simple_layer); backed ones repaint their whole area (backed_resize). CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: own layer during the blur fade (MorphPanelOpt sub-claim 2; v1 g0.1b)
notes.text: why-engines: the tween's first frame attaches a new backing store (setNeedsDisplay over the whole bounds, PlatformCALayerRemote.mm:719-731@862f17d; no front buffer, so full display, ImageBufferSet.cpp:42-50), so it adds the element's area to resident memory and paints at least that area (promote_tween). CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: own clock layer: the clock wrapper in the menu centre composited while the menu is open (KD#12 menuClock.ownLayer; v1 panel-clock-layer and g0.0i)
notes.text: why-engines (WebKit half, statement refuted): a store paints only its dirty rect when its front buffer is valid and partial repaint is supported, copying the rest forward from the back buffer (ImageBufferSet.cpp:103-147@862f17d); it paints the whole store only with no or purged front buffer, or when partial repaint is off, which happens for backends <= 64x64 px (ImageBufferSet.cpp:42-56, RemoteLayerBackingStore.mm:293-307). So in the steady state D_wk(o) = a, not B, and an own layer cannot paint less (host_steady_le_own). CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: MQ-gated shrink (KD#3): skip the --future-shrink write and the rAF re-request in the c860 band
notes.text: why-engines: custom properties live in the inherited rare data (StyleInheritedRareData.h:153@862f17d), so a changed value is Change::Inherited (StyleChange.cpp:42-43) and the resolver restyles every child, passing on through each child whose style changes (StyleTreeResolver.cpp:283-311, 1185-1212). Style units = 1 + |reached| (custom_style_units), and skipping the write is strictly less work (customSkip_lt). CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: blur tail cut 1.6 s -> 0.9 s via a 17-stop linear() resample, then snap to none (KD#15, large-area-blur)
notes.text: why-engines (statement over-strong, corrected): KeyframeEffectStack::allowsAcceleration fails if any effect preventsAcceleration, or on implicit-keyframe overlap or a threaded/non-threaded mix on a shared accelerated property (KeyframeEffectStack.cpp:215-283@862f17d), then stops every effect (:285-300) (stack_rule). preventsAcceleration is false on the threaded path and for an effect that animates no accelerated property and has no motion path (KeyframeEffect.cpp:2035-2058), so a non-accelerable main-thread effect such as a background animation does not stop the stack (stack_free, stackDemo guard). CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: rest at opacity 0.999 and scale(1) so no presence flip happens (st6, KD#8)
notes.text: why-engines: opacity < 1 makes the box a stacking context (computed_style.h:2085, computed_style.cc:2958-2995@f842f52); a flip of that bit asks for full layout and paint invalidation (computed_style.cc:779-784), unless another reason keeps the box a stacking context. So 1 -> 0.999 costs layoutFull (opacityCross1_layout) and resting at 0.999 is never above the plain opacity row (rest999_le). CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: cqiFormula sizing (g0.0j): aspect-ratio + height:auto -> container-type:inline-size + height:calc(100cqi*764/353)
notes.text: why-engines (statement corrected): a reached size container skips its descendants and queues a container query state (StyleTreeResolver.cpp:1377, 1391-1394, 1460-1478@862f17d); resolve() asks for another round (:1515-1522) and Document::resolveStyle runs a layout between rounds only if the render tree needs one (Document.cpp:2897-2911). So a reached container costs >= 2 style rounds (wkRounds_ge_two) but layouts only when layout-dirty (wkLayouts_le); 'layout passes >= 1' was wrong. CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: no container-type above per-frame text (platform.containers off)
notes.text: why-engines (statement corrected): the rounds are style rounds, WebKit 1 + max reached-container depth (StyleTreeResolver.cpp:1460-1478, 1515-1522; Document.cpp:2897-2911@862f17d), Chromium 1 + max layout-dirty container depth, resumed inside the one layout pass (element.cc:5187-5225, 5360-5375@f842f52). Removing a container never adds a round in either engine (wkRounds_remove, crRounds_remove), but lowers WebKit's only if it is on a deepest chain, not iff c in trav(f) (wkRounds_not_iff). CONFIRMED.

notes.entry: own layer during the blur fade (MorphPanelOpt sub-claim 2; v1 g0.1b)
notes.text: engine-model-fix: sign change, Chromium trade -> no-win. Mechanism: Chromium re-rasters a layer whose blur radius changes even when the layer is its own (CI run 39088367495: filter(blur)@own and scale@own run RasterTask, 3 of 3 passes); the old model put a blur on an own layer at ppFull (property-tree update only) and so credited the own layer with raster -1 per fade frame. Lean why: Fw.Parts.MorphPanelOpt.cr_fade_stages (the fade write is the raster level on every layer state), cr_fade_eq (equal frame work), cr_fade_noClaim (claim = noClaim; the own layer only adds fade_layers_up). WebKit stays a trade with a new mechanism (paint -1, props -1, wk_fade_trade). General lesson: promoting an element only helps the stages that its change can skip on the compositor; a filter whose parameters change re-rasters on the main thread whatever the layer, so promotion buys memory cost, no work.

notes.entry: blur(0) -> filter:none at rest (MorphPanelOpt rest variant)
notes.text: engine-model-fix: sign change, WebKit trade -> win. Mechanism: the WebKit cost was the rest<->fade toggle frame, modelled as +1 layout unit for the variant's none<->blur flip; but the original's blur(0)<->blur(x) value change also lays out, because a filter change with new outsets is a Layout-level StyleDifference (CI run 39088367495: filter at layer and own runs layoutUpdates). Lean why: Fw.Parts.MorphPanelOpt.wk_toggle_layout_units (2 layout units in both arms), wk_toggle_eqv (equal toggle frames), with wk_rest_claim (rest frames dominate) and wk_rest_layers (one layer fewer). The run-level WebKit statement is not yet one theorem (missingWhy). Chromium stays a trade (cr_toggle_not_le). General lesson: before charging a threshold toggle to the variant, check what the original's continuous change at the same frame already pays; a value change that moves geometry (outsets) costs the same layout as the on/off flip.

In the model it holds over a whole swipe of rest, toggle and fade frames in any order: Fw.Parts.MorphPanelOpt.wk_cross_claim (claim = dominates, from wk_cross_le: rest by wk_rest_le, toggle by wk_toggle_eqv, fade frames equal by filterV_fade; and wk_cross_resident: the variant never keeps more layers or backing). notes.entry: g0.0b: the rAF tween replaced by one WAAPI animation on a registered --morph with cubic-bezier(1/3,1,2/3,1)
notes.text: Finding (CONFIRMED by source: Chromium custom_property.cc:22-23@f842f52, WebKit StyleBuilder.cpp:496-505@862f17d; not observed by the gate, m = 0 only): the waapi arm registered --morph with inherits:false, so every reader below the animated nav (the hosted morph panel at depth 1, .logo and .actions at 2, .btn.earn at 3) took the initial value 0 and never saw the tween; the waapi arm had never been gated for port-morph-tween. Fix: Lean MT-R in Fw.Parts.MorphTweenOpt decides the registrations (registrations_rule: inherits iff a reader sits below the element or the original inherits; registrations_see: every reader sees the animated value; panel_blind_without_inherit: the bug), and the TS REGISTRATIONS are checked against the golden rows. --morph is now <number> inherits:true initial 0. Work claim survives (morph_scope_eq): an inherited registration recomputes the same elements and values as the original's unregistered --morph (Chromium custom_property.cc:22-23@f842f52, WebKit StyleBuilder.cpp:103-106@862f17d), so MT-W keeps one change list for both arms; the waapi arm also animates --morph on the platform section, whose subtree both arms already invalidate every frame through the inherited --morph-fade (Chromium computed_style.cc:472-475@f842f52); inherits:false would recalc fewer elements but render a wrong picture. Second finding (MEASURED, run 39184893562): on chromium the platform section's inline --morph-fade (unregistered) computed to the text calc(1 - min(1, 0 / 0.55)) against the original's 1; registering --morph-fade <number> inherits:true initial 1 fixes it. Gate after the fix: default arm run 39187616419 and fw=morph.tween:waapi run 39187623386: morph.mount/countdown/columns/tween/panel and platform rows pass in every reachable cell (webkit: 2 columns UNREACHABLE 4, same on both arms); chromium verdict pass on both (default 7048 pass, 1 fail, 8 excused of 7056; waapi 7049 pass, 0 fail, 7 excused of 7056); webkit incomplete on both (6763 pass, 0 fail, 291 excused of 7056) only for matchMedia phone-rotation not-comparable (unrelated). Engine-check run 39131146372 (?fw=morph.tween:waapi) measured the inherits:false build and predates this change. Limit: the gate checks static states at m = 0 only (no wheel push), where initial and animated values agree, so it could not see the panel bug; the Lean proof and the golden test carry it. Keeping waapi in v2-proved is a lead decision.

notes.text: hero-exit-threaded-measure (WebKit cost lane, MEASURED): webkit-sim dispatches with lag=true cost=on target=rewrite vms=3 on the iOS Simulator 430x775 (no real GPU), base against ?fw=hero.exit:threaded, zone hero exit (scroll A), per scroll step: base run 39739724461 (VMs r1 and r3, 4 passes; r2 lost its page target and the Simulator shut down), flag run 39731192687 (r1 r2 r3, 6 passes). requestAnimationFrame callbacks 6.88 to 5.88 (every pass, deterministic), Layout events 7.80 to 6.51, Recalculate styles events 7.52 to 6.46, each with the per-pass ranges separated (Lean WebKitLag.verdict); adding the 2 passes of run 39731185714 to the base changes no per-step verdict. Recalculate styles time relative to each arm's calm baseline is lower with the flag: ratio 1.89 (1.78-2.02) against 1.27 (1.15-1.54), FunctionCall time 1.55 (1.30-1.67) against 1.13 (0.99-1.28), both separated (FunctionCall time overlaps with the 6 base passes); per-step InvalidateLayout 7.95 to 5.95, ScheduleStyleRecalculation 7.42 to 6.42, FireAnimationFrame 6.69 to 5.75 also separated; the calm baselines are equal (12,735 and 12,935 us) and flag r3 alone on the base's runner image gives the same verdicts. Absolute per-step Recalculate styles time, Layout time, FunctionCall, Paint, skipped display slots (78.9 against 81.8 per 100 frames), frames over 50 ms, Paint and Composite per frame, new and resized layers per read: ranges overlap, no difference shown. Backing store 51.6 against 54.5 MB at scroll state 2, layer count overlaps. Mechanism: INFERRED that the exit script and its forced track-rect layout and style pass are the removed events (the counts are MEASURED); the remaining style events (6.46 per step) equal the same arm's calm-scroll baseline (6.45), and WebKit still restyles scroll-timeline targets once per rendering update when accelerated (note wktr-p1p4), so one event out of about seven per step does not show in the absolute per-step time, where the Simulator passes spread, and shows only against the calm baseline. Result: one script callback, one layout and one style pass fewer per step and a lower style time relative to the calm scroll; absolute times and cadence do not separate in this lane; the felt effect is open (phone replay). Lesson: read a zone against the same arm's calm baseline as well as in absolute cells; a removed main-thread event is never proof of smoother frames, so judge the feel on the phone. Open: the page is 36 px longer with the flag (maxY 5231 against 5267), check it in the phone replay. Note research/notes/2026/10-2x-hero-exit-threaded-measure.md; limits: no real GPU, one width, runner images differ between arms (same-image check: flag r3), entrance not sampled (Lean entrance_same and unit tests).

notes.entry: morph.end.release:on (brick C of morph-end-bricks): a close start drops the pin and stops preventDefault until the next open
notes.text: combo-scroll-fight: CONFIRMED a bug of release alone, not of its composition with arm-late or unthrottle. A close start is not prevented, so the page scrolls natively and every later touchmove of that touch is not cancelable; a reopen in such a move pins the page at the scroll position it reads and the frame writer then writes that pin against the finger and the fling. MEASURED on CI Chromium (run 40130709244, build before the fix): release alone fought in 13 of 16 replays, clamp alone, flip alone and the user's flags minus release in 0 of 15, the user's flags minus arm-late or minus unthrottle in 12 of 15. PROVED in Lean (Fw.Parts.ComboScroll: native_quiet, wrap_all_hold, wstep_off, wtrace_decisions): a hold bit (last move prevented and cancelable) gates the one frame writer; every brick theorem holds with it. After the fix the same replays: 0 script writes, 0 no-finger reversals, 0 script jumps of 20 px or more in 15-16 of 15-16 replays per release arm. Note research/notes/2026/10-2x-combo-scroll-fight.md. Look: look change added to release: a reopen in a move the page cannot cancel opens the morph and leaves the page to the finger; the pin returns at the next prevented, cancelable move, so an open morph can sit over a page that scrolled away from the end until the next touch. The user's phone review decides. Next: phone re-check by the user. Follow-ups: the waapi drivers pin without the bit; the toolbar-resize fight at y about 1859 (held pin written while the viewport height changes, INFERRED, not reproducible without a toolbar); the faithful page keeps the original's pin against a fling at the page end (default arm, recorded path).

notes.text: one-chain-webkit: restated: the +1 forced recalc and +10 elements of swipe-touch-v1 frame 499 are the first build's digit position. The digits ran at their shared subscriber, before the scroll engine's tick (added after it by the scroll event, which runs before the rAF callbacks: Chromium page_animator.cc:266-340@f842f52, WebKit Page.cpp:2294-2329@862f17d). The tick's first read window.scrollY flushes dirty style (Chromium local_dom_window.cc:1877@f842f52; WebKit LocalDOMWindow.cpp:1476-1480@862f17d), so the 10 face writes got their own update, and the tick's later subtree restyle (320 elements, faces included) visited them again: 2 updates, 330 elements against 1 and 320 (CONFIRMED by the counts of runs 39313842964 and 39313910496 and by Lean frame499_faithful and frame499_atSubscriber, which give 1/320 and 2/330 for f = 10, m = 320; 531-frame profile only; that the scroll tick is the reader is INFERRED, the counts lane has no stacks). Digits last fixes frame 499 (Lean frame499_last) but adds one empty update in 157 of 771 frames (MEASURED, 3 of 3 runs; Lean early_last: +1 update, equal elements), because the original's digits run before the shared loop in those frames. Lean no_fixed_order (a model result): in the model no fixed position wins both frame kinds, so the variant stays at the subscribe position (lead decision; MEASURED round 2: +1 update in 233-238 of 771 frames, more than digits last's 157-159 on the same profile). Golden row orders. See research/notes/2026/10-2x-one-chain-webkit.md. || Round 2 (head f74e3313a): UpdateLayoutTree +283 (2392 to 2675, +11.8 %), ScheduleStyleRecalculation +284, elements equal (60180 vs 60155), FireAnimationFrame -314 (2572 to 2258); the extra update is +1 in 233-238 of 771 frames in the same ranges in all runs, so Lean early_atSubscriber (no extra update) is falsified for this base and the early-frame kind stays a fit (INFERRED). Verdict Chromium: trade (MEASURED). Gate with the flag, run 40153922711: all pass. Summaries results/one-chain-webkit/summary.json. WebKit: RecalculateStyles 672.3 (654-692) base vs 671.8 (652-693) flag, Layout 627.2 vs 644.3 (inside the base spread 603-664), FireAnimationFrame 672.7 vs 676.3.
